seller_questions: What is the VIN? I'd like to run a history report before viewing.
Have the rod bearings ever been replaced? If so, can you send the invoice with date and mileage?
Has an oil analysis (e.g., Blackstone) been done in the last few years? Can you share the report?
Has the rear subframe / trunk floor been inspected or reinforced? Can you send photos of the trunk floor with the carpet lifted, around the differential mounts?
Which shop did the 'professional maintenance'? Can you share dated invoices for cooling-system work, VANOS, brake fluid and coolant changes?
What are the DOT date codes and brand of the 'new' tires, and is there a receipt?
How long have you owned the car, and how many owners does the title show? Is the title clean and in your name?
Will you provide a current California smog certificate at sale?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, including the first 30 seconds of idle?
Is the car being sold by you privately or on consignment at the dealership where it was photographed?
Will you allow a pre-purchase inspection at a local independent BMW shop, including a lift inspection and scan?
ppi_focus: Rear subframe and trunk floor: remove the trunk carpet, check spot welds and differential mount ears for cracks or tearing, inspect from below for prior welding or reinforcement plates.
S54 bottom end: pull an oil sample for analysis (copper/lead) and check filter media for bearing material; listen for a knock on cold start.
VANOS: scan with BMW-capable software for VANOS faults, check solenoid/pump function and exhaust hub, and listen for rattle at idle and on throttle tip-in.
Cooling system: pressure test, inspect radiator end tanks, expansion tank, water pump weep and hoses; confirm temperature stability on the drive.
Oil leaks: valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket, rear main seal / oil pan.
Rear trailing-arm bushings, rear shock mounts, motor and transmission mounts, and differential condition.
Rust at rockers, floors and jacking points, plus evidence of accident repair (paint meter, panel gaps).
Soft top and hardtop: seals, rear window, top mechanism, and a water-leak check given year-round rain use.
Clutch engagement point, slip test, and flywheel chatter; shifter bushings.
Tire DOT codes, brake pad/rotor condition, and full cluster check for warning lights and pixel faults.
what_would_change_verdict: Documented rod-bearing replacement (or a clean recent oil analysis) plus trunk-floor photos showing intact or reinforced differential mounts would materially raise documentation and condition.
A clean-title history report with one or two owners and dated cooling/VANOS invoices would strengthen the case.
A price closer to the fair-value range, or a reduction reflecting a needed bearing job, would improve value.
Any evidence of subframe cracking, a branded title, an accident, or metal in the oil analysis would move it sharply down.
evidence.mission_note: A manual S54 Z3 M with a hardtop fits Jason's candidate list and the year-round brief, and it is local and inspectable. As a future-keeper purchase, though, it currently offers no documentation of the S54 and rear-structure risks that would justify paying over fair value, and it carries notably higher running costs than an MX-5 RF.
evidence.rationale: The listing photo-verifies a 2001 Z3 M Roadster with the S54 engine, 5-speed manual, 94,319 miles, and both soft top and hardtop. It is located in Monterey, close to Jason. Everything else rests on seller prose: 'professionally maintained', 'new battery and tires', with no VIN, title, owner or accident data and no receipts. None of the three model-critical items is evidenced: S54 rod bearings at 94k miles, rear subframe / trunk-floor condition, and cooling-system history. Photos show an apparently stock engine bay, healthy-looking tires and age-appropriate seat wear, plus minor non-original items (Kenwood head unit, grille stripe insert). The $20,000 ask is above the $14,740–$19,093 fair-value range, partly offset by the included hardtop and the S54. Proximity means every open question can be answered quickly with a VIN check and a local specialist PPI.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller asking for the VIN, any rod-bearing/cooling/VANOS invoices, and trunk-floor photos with the carpet lifted, and confirm they will allow a PPI at a local independent BMW shop.
